answer: Each new identity must lock a non-transferable registration bond, slashable if the same hardware root later appears under a second key. Established peers will countersign only a live work signal bound to that unique root, so a farm cannot recycle one machine across many aliases without triggering the slash. The bond is priced like scarce saffron: affordable for a single honest registrant, ruinous when multiplied across a swarm. A public marble ledger records failed fingerprints so later issuers reject them automatically.
